Ceperognastat fails its clinical endpoint; higher dose worsens progression

The OGA-inhibitor trial found biomarker changes without clinical benefit, with worse outcomes at the higher dose.

Important new evidence•Peer-reviewed randomized trial•July 13, 2026

Ceperognastat fails its clinical endpoint; higher dose worsens progression

The OGA-inhibitor trial found biomarker changes without clinical benefit, with worse outcomes at the higher dose.

Key quantitative results: At week 100, iADRS differences versus placebo were +1.68 (95% credible interval −0.375 to 3.771) with 0.75 mg and −3.20 (−5.354 to −1.042) with 3 mg; positive values favor treatment.

BiomarkersManagementBloodp-tau217GFAPDisease-modifying treatment

Added September 7, 2026 · DOI:10.1001/jama.2026.12768

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Clinical outcomes must govern interpretation of favorable biomarker movement.

Study design

PROSPECT-ALZ randomized 327 participants with early symptomatic AD. The primary low-to-medium-tau population comprised 259 participants.

Key quantitative results

  • At week 100, iADRS differences versus placebo were +1.68 (95% credible interval −0.375 to 3.771) with 0.75 mg and −3.20 (−5.354 to −1.042) with 3 mg; positive values favor treatment.
  • The prespecified primary success criterion was missed by both doses. The high-dose progression ratio was 1.32 (95% credible interval 1.10–1.58), indicating 32% greater progression.

What changed

A controlled trial identifies clinical harm despite target engagement.

Strength of evidence

Randomized evidence; model-based primary analysis.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Does not support ceperognastat treatment.

Field medical relevance

Useful counterexample to surrogate-only efficacy claims.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Biomarker effects are not proof of patient benefit.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No clinical access recommendation.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Are these confidence intervals?
They are Bayesian credible intervals from the primary model.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Variable exposure, differential discontinuation and limited diversity.
  • Results cannot be generalized to every tau-directed mechanism.

Primary source · DOI

Fleisher AS, Munsie L, Mancini M, et al. Ceperognastat in early symptomatic Alzheimer disease. JAMA. July 13, 2026. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.12768.
